messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from yesterday's postmortem on the repeated cache-eviction incidents. Goal: ship small, actionable runbook edits that reduce time-to-mitigation and clarify who does what. Need: a 5-step quick triage, copy-paste ops commands, escalation matrix with timeboxes, and telemetry thresholds. Who can take which?

sara: I can own the quick triage. Draft idea: 1) ID scope (single model vs cluster), 2) check kvcache hit/miss deltas, 3) check eviction reason code, 4) apply temporary mitigation (scale/cache settings), 5) notify & tag incident. Will write it concise.

jordan: I'll add concrete commands and example outputs. Proposed snippets (exact text to paste):
```sh
# recent eviction events
redwoodctl telemetry events list --type eviction --since 20m --json

# kvcache KPI snapshot
redwoodctl metrics query "kvcache_hit_rate{job=\"runtime\"}[5m]"

# pod health + mem
kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide --selector=app=runtime
kubectl exec -n redwood $(kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -o name | head -n1) -- cat /proc/meminfo | head

# tail recent runtime errors
kubectl logs -n redwood -l app=runtime -c runtime --since=10m | tail -n 200
```

mike: For escalation: propose timeline: ack by oncall within 10m, engage eng-sre within 20m if not mitigated, inform eng-runtime by 40m, and CC platform leads + customer-sre at 90m. I'll assemble a role-based contact table (primary/secondary) and confirm rotation overlap.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-1437 created and linked. Reminder: owners should post PRs in the `playbooks/` repo and link here.

sara: Adding mitigation recipes to triage: if hit-rate drops >30% and evictions spike -> increase kvcache shard_limit by 20% and restart cache pods one-at-a-time. If eviction reason == "oom" -> reduce model batch size or route traffic to model-compact. Example command: `redwoodctl config patch kvcache --shard-limit +20% --reason "postmortem-mitigation"`

jordan: Telemetry examples I'll include: grafana expression for hit-rate: `increase(kvcache_hits_total[5m]) / increase(kvcache_requests_total[5m])` and a 95th token-latency alert: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 300` (ms).

laura: Nice. Let's assign owners & deadlines: sara -> publish 5-step triage doc + short mitigation recipes (due: 2 business days), jordan -> compile commands + telemetry queries + sample outputs (due: 3 business days), mike -> escalation matrix + contact table + rotation verification (due: 4 business days). I'll run a 20-minute check-in 48 hours from now.

alex: Add one small playbook rule: if uncertain whether issue is cache-layer or model memory, prefer conservative action: reduce traffic to suspect model before mass restarts. Also flag recurrent patterns for a follow-on investigation ticket.

mike: I'll also add SLA targets into the playbook: 10m ack, 30m temporary mitigation, 2h full remediation ETA for critical customer impact.

sara: ACK. I'll start a draft PR and tag @jordan for command validation.

jordan: ACK. I'll paste example logs and a small troubleshooting table (eviction reasons -> suggested next steps).

oncall-bot: Reminder set: runbook PRs due in 5 days.

laura: Summary (copy/paste):
- sara: 5-step triage + mitigation snippets (due in 2bd)
- jordan: ops commands + telemetry queries + example outputs (due in 3bd)
- mike: escalation matrix + contact table + SLA entries (due in 4bd)
Please reply here to confirm ownership and ETA. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks everyone. We'll mark this as high-priority runbook follow-up and track in the postmortem action tracker.
